seo.title: Karmic tail 18 9 9 compatibility: The Moon and two Hermits
seo.description: Karmic tail 18 9 9 compatibility in the destiny matrix: a shared secret at the entry, a path walked apart and the task of not letting solitude become silence.

title: Karmic tail 18-9-9 in compatibility: a secret for two and the task of not falling silent
short: The karmic tail 18-9-9 in destiny matrix compatibility is The Moon at the entry to the task and The Hermit twice: in the middle and in the main task. The couple comes together over a secret only the two of them understand, walks the path apart, each with a lantern of their own, and its main task is to keep solitude from turning into silence.

paragraphs: In early twelfth-century Paris the most famous teacher was Peter Abelard. The most learned young woman in the kingdom was Heloise, niece of the canon Fulbert. Abelard set out to win her, and later, in his Historia calamitatum, he explained why he chose her. One of the reasons: "so, even if we were parted, we might yet be together in thought with the aid of written messages. Perchance, too, we might be able to write more boldly than we could speak".

The whole tail is already in that sentence. "To write more boldly than we could speak" is the language of The Moon: things said in half-light, not face to face. "Even if we were parted" is The Hermit, who has not arrived yet but is already on his mind. Abelard provided for separation before the first meeting. Some fifteen years later it came true to the letter: the two lived in two monasteries and wrote to each other. Only the first letter that arrived was not about love. It was about silence.

This article does not claim that an 18-9-9 couple is headed for a monastery. The cards do not predict events: no partings, no catastrophes, no dates. What matches is the mechanism — a secret at the entry, withdrawal in the middle, silence as the main task. It is worth taking apart step by step: the evidence is in the letters, in Waite's and Wen's books and in the numbers themselves.

sections.h2: Entry to the task, 18 — The Moon: "secret retreats"
paragraphs: The first point of a couple's tail is what the two want together: shared wishes, agreements, a common language. On the site the same point also appears in the sphere "Relationship and common language" under the label "Common language". For an 18-9-9 couple the common language is The Moon. The point lies on the line of tasks, so the same wish can also become resistance.

For Abelard and Heloise the common language was lessons. Fulbert took the famous teacher into his house and entrusted his niece to him, to be taught "no matter whether by day or by night". Abelard says he was astounded by such simplicity: it was as if the uncle "had entrusted a tender lamb to the care of a ravenous wolf". Then: "Under the pretext of study we spent our hours in the happiness of love, and learning held out to us the secret opportunities that our passion craved. Our speech was more of love than of the book which lay open before us".

Abelard's Latin is sharper: secretos regressus, "secret retreats". Two words — a secret and a retreat — and the tail fits into one phrase: The Moon's secrecy and The Hermit's withdrawal. From the very start the two withdrew not from each other but together, from everyone else.

The Moon has a strange property: a secret for two quickly becomes a rumour for all. Abelard wrote songs about his love, and, as he says, "some have become widely known and have been sung in many lands". Only one man failed to guess: the thing "could deceive only a few, no one, methinks, save him whose shame it chiefly bespoke, the girl's uncle, Fulbert". Everyone found out except the one they were hiding from.

Then the entry turns into resistance. When the secret came out, Abelard offered to marry, on one condition: "provided only the thing could be kept secret". They were married early in the morning after a night of prayer in a church, before the uncle and a few friends. When Fulbert's household began to talk about the marriage, Heloise, Abelard writes, "swore that they were speaking the most absolute lies". Every cover demanded the next one: the lessons hid the love, the secret marriage hid the love from gossip, and the nun's habit in which Abelard himself dressed Heloise at Argenteuil hid the wife from her family's anger. The end came at night: Fulbert's people bribed a servant and mutilated Abelard in his sleep.

Among the tasks of a couple with The Moon, Lisovskaya names an image created at the start which later collapses. Abelard and Heloise created that image not for each other but together, for the world. The same often holds for an 18-9-9 couple: The Moon at the entry is less a deception of the partner than a shared conspiracy against outsiders.

In today's life it looks familiar. An affair kept from colleagues for six months. A relationship the parents learned about last. Messages in which both are bolder than at dinner: confessions in writing, jokes in person. Private nicknames, private words, the feeling of being read without words. That is the strength of The Moon: intuition, play, a world for two. The weakness grows from the same root: the agreement "we don't talk about the important things" first hides the couple from the world and then starts working inside it. Jealousy over an invented story, hurt over words the partner never said — that is The Moon too, only turned inward.

sections.h2: Middle of the task, 9 — The Hermit: "by separate ways"
paragraphs: Lisovskaya gives the middle of a couple's tail no meaning of its own: it is an "addition" to the main task. In our reading the middle shows how the couple walks from the shared wish to the main task. For 18-9-9 that road runs through The Hermit, through each partner withdrawing into their own.

For Abelard the middle begins on the day of the wedding. Straight after the secret ceremony, he writes, "We departed forthwith stealthily and by separate ways, nor thereafter did we see each other save rarely and in private". From the shared secret to the main task the road runs through two separate doors.

The Hermit in the middle is not necessarily coldness. After their first parting, when Fulbert learned everything, Abelard writes: "Each grieved most, not for himself, but for the other", and "The very sundering of our bodies served but to link our souls closer together". Distance can bring people closer. In Lisovskaya's description the positive Hermit looks quite ordinary: each has a corner of the home and an hour of quiet, and love shows in deeds rather than words.

Then came two monasteries, Saint-Denis and Argenteuil. Abelard withdrew to wasteland near Troyes and there "built with reeds and stalks" an oratory. Students followed him, built huts above the river Arduzon, "so that they seemed hermits rather than scholars". Abelard named the oratory the Paraclete — Greek for "the Consoler". At Argenteuil Heloise became the head of her community. Each grew into a lantern of their own.

The danger of the middle is time. A pause that was chosen becomes the default. Two people at two desks, in two pairs of headphones. One on shifts, the other studying. A long-distance relationship where "we don't call every day, and we're fine". It really is fine while the quiet remains a choice. The tail tests something else: whether the two will notice when it stops being one.

sections.h2: Main task, 9 — The Hermit: a consolation sent to a friend
paragraphs: The main point of a couple's tail is its task and trial; Lisovskaya reads it mostly through its weak side. For 18-9-9 it is The Hermit again, but in another role: the middle shows the path, the task shows what has to be learned on it.

In 1129 the nuns were driven out of Argenteuil, and Abelard made over his Paraclete to Heloise, "together with everything pertaining thereto". A few years later he wrote the Historia calamitatum as a letter of consolation to an unnamed friend. The letter reached Heloise. Her reply is the central scene of this tail.

"You wrote your friend a long letter of consolation, about his misfortunes indeed, but about your own. Recalling them so carefully in order to console him, you have greatly added to our desolation." And then: "Tell me one thing, if you can: why, after our entry into religion, which you alone decided on, have I fallen into such neglect and oblivion with you that I am neither refreshed by your talk when you are here nor consoled by your letters when you are away?" (Heloise's letters are quoted in our translation from the Latin.)

The man who named his retreat the Consoler and wrote a consolation to a friend did not console the one closest to him. He knew the weight of that word himself. Having left the Paraclete to become an abbot in Brittany, he wrote: "Justly has this sorrow come upon me because I deserted the Paraclete, which is to say the Consoler, and thrust myself into sure desolation". In Heloise's Latin the words rhyme: his consolatio for a friend became her desolatio — comfort for one turned into desolation for the other.

In Lisovskaya, the weak side of The Hermit in a couple is the same picture: trouble piles up in silence, and when things get hard each retreats into their own shell instead of reaching out a hand. Heloise adds a precise image: "You tend a vineyard of another man's vines, which you did not plant… Consider what you owe to your own, you who spend such care on another's."

In a modern couple the letter to a friend looks like this. She learns how hard his autumn was from his conversation with a friend. He learns about her doubts from her own post. There is light, but it burns for others: colleagues, students, clients, followers. At home it is quiet and polite.

sections.h2: "Do not think me strong": how the trap closes
paragraphs: Abelard replied. His first sentence is the most recognisable line of this tail: "If since our conversion from the world to God I have not yet written you any word of comfort or exhortation, this must be put down not to my negligence but to your wisdom, in which I have always had the greatest confidence. I was sure it needed nothing of the kind" (our translation).

In today's words it is shorter: "You're strong, you'll manage." Heloise had answered that before she heard it: "the more secure I have made you, the more neglect I have to bear." And in her second letter, directly: "Do not think me strong, or I may fall before you can hold me up as I slip." And again: "Always fear for me, I beg you, rather than trust in me, so that your care may always help me."

This is the mechanism of the main task. In a couple whose task is The Hermit, respect for the other's independence quietly becomes a reason not to ask. Trust turns into inattention, and inattention looks like trust. Lisovskaya puts the task her own way: to sense when to support and when to leave the other in peace. Abelard chose "leave in peace" where "support" was needed, and sincerely believed it was respect.

There is a second half to the trap. Abelard gave Heloise his retreat with everything in it: The Hermit's love is shown in deeds. She asked for something else: "In vain do I hope for you to be generous in deeds if I find you a miser with words." A renovated flat, a car, paid-for courses — and not one "how are you?". In an 18-9-9 couple one partner often gives in deeds while the other waits for words.

And one more detail without which the story is not honest. Heloise was hiding too. The flawless abbess whom bishops praised writes: "Men call me chaste because they have not found out the hypocrite", and to Abelard: "For a long time my pretence deceived you, as it deceived many, so that you took hypocrisy for piety." The silence was double: he kept his troubles from her, she kept her real self behind the image of a model abbess. In an 18-9-9 couple either partner can be the silent one, and more often both take turns.

Heloise's comparison shows how the tail changed from entry to task: "When long ago you sought me for base pleasures, you visited me with letter after letter, and with song after song you put your Heloise on every tongue." The Moon spoke easily — in hints, songs and letters. The Hermit fell silent. The main task is to bring the words back without giving up the solitude.

sections.h2: The Moon and The Hermit in Waite and Wen
paragraphs: In Waite's divinatory list the reversed Moon includes the word silence: "Instability, inconstancy, silence, lesser degrees of deception and error". A calculated number is never reversed, and this is no verdict on the couple. But the vocabulary is telling: The Moon already knows silence, and The Hermit will make it a task.

Benebell Wen separates The Moon from The High Priestess with a pair of sentences: "Key 2 is about disguise. Key 18 is about revelation of the inner self". The Priestess is disguise, The Moon is the inner self coming out. For a couple that matters: The Moon at the entry is not a card of deceit but a card of what has not been said yet and is asking to come out.

Of the crayfish crawling out of the water on Waite's Moon card, Wen writes: "there is a sense of needing to feel protected, and thus forming the tough outer shell. Simultaneously, there is a profound vulnerability that the Seeker is trying to conceal from others". A tough shell and a vulnerability hidden under it. In Lisovskaya, the task of a couple with The Hermit is not to hide "in one's shell" when things get hard. The Moon's shell and The Hermit's shell are one and the same defence. The mask of the flawless abbess was such a shell, and "do not think me strong" was the vulnerability finally coming ashore.
On the same Waite card a dog and a wolf bay at the moon. Describing the beginning, Abelard called himself the wolf.

Wen describes The Hermit this way: "The Hermit is a guardian of higher thoughts and contemplation". The word "guardian" will come back. And in Waite's divinatory list The Hermit has, besides prudence, dissimulation — the very pretence Heloise confessed to.

sections.h2: A room with two cards: the evidence in the numbers
paragraphs: The 18-9-9 tail occurs in 1.754% of couples, about one in 57; it ranks 18th of the 97 couple tails. The site's engine shows more: this tail locks the couple inside two cards.

The Moon and The Hermit are the only cards from 1 to 22 divisible by nine. Reducing a number to 22 by adding its digits does not change its remainder after division by nine. And the inner points of the matrix are all derived from the main task: by that remainder the centre equals two main tasks, the entry three, the middle four and the values six. If the main task is divisible by nine, so is everything else. That is why, in a couple with The Hermit as the main task, the entry, the middle, the centre and "The couple's values" can only be The Moon or The Hermit. The arithmetic lets no other card in.

Every ninth couple is built this way: in 11.1% the main task is The Hermit or The Moon. There are eight tails made only of these two cards, and all eight occur. 18-9-9 is the third most frequent of them, after 9-9-18 and 9-9-9.

What this means for the atmosphere. The couple's centre, that is "The atmosphere inside the couple", is The Moon in 57.1% of 18-9-9 couples and The Hermit in 42.9%. "The couple's values" are The Hermit in 64.3% and The Moon in 35.7%. Together: in 36.4% of couples The Moon is in the centre and The Hermit in the values, in 27.9% The Hermit is in both, in 20.7% The Moon is in both, and in 15% The Hermit is in the centre and The Moon in the values. With The Moon in the centre the partner is a friend first and understanding comes without words, while on the weak side it is unclear whether the two are friends or rivals, and secrets become weapons. With The Hermit in the centre each has a corner and a time of their own, while on the weak side each lives on their own.
When Lisovskaya reads a couple's tail, she adds its energies in pairs and all three together. The Moon and The Hermit give 18 + 9 = 27, which is 9 again. Two Hermits give 18, The Moon.
Now add up all three numbers.
18 + 9 + 9 = 36, and 3 + 6 = 9. No combination leads out of the two cards: the tail keeps returning to itself, like two people walking from cell to cell.

Where these cards come from in the two partners. The 18-9-9 tail is formed by five combinations of the partners' personal tails. Most often these are 15-20-5 and 3-7-22 (34% of such couples), 12-19-7 and 6-8-20 (26%), 15-5-8 and 3-22-19 (24%). In 83% of couples neither partner has The Moon or The Hermit in their personal tail: this room appears only between them. In 16%, couples with the personal tails 9-12-3 and 9-15-6, both personal tails begin with a nine, and two Hermits together give The Moon at the couple's entry.

sections.h2: An example: how a couple gets 18-9-9
paragraphs: Take two dates: 07.08.1976 and 05.07.1975. The first partner's personal tail is 6-8-20, the second's is 12-19-7. Each point of the couple is the sum of the matching points of the two personal matrices, reduced to 22 if the sum is larger.

The couple's middle is calculated from the partners' middles, not from the two outer numbers of the couple. Here the result would be the same, but the rule is different, and in other couples the difference shows.

In this couple The Hermit reaches far beyond the tail. The centre is 4 + 5 = 9. "The couple's values" are also 9: they are recalculated from the couple's own sums, not added from the partners' values (3 and 15 would give The Moon). Further:

sections.h2: The strong version: guardians of solitude
paragraphs: For Abelard and Heloise the correspondence did not end in reproach. In his first reply Abelard wrote: "write to me about whatever you wish, so that I may answer you" (our translation). Heloise began to ask, and never stopped. She asked him to tell how communities of women began and to write a rule for a women's house; Abelard wrote both. For the Paraclete he composed hymns. Later Heloise sent him forty-two questions on difficult passages of Scripture, and he answered every one. The two remained hermits, each in their own monastery. But their solitude became a conversation.

Heloise became a lantern herself. Abelard writes of her as head of the Paraclete: "The less often she allowed herself to be seen, shutting herself up in her cell to devote herself to sacred meditations and prayers, the more eagerly did those who dwelt without demand her presence and the spiritual guidance of her words." His retreat became her home, and, in his own words, "the place proved itself a true Paraclete to them". When Abelard died in 1142, his body was secretly carried to the Paraclete. Later Heloise was buried beside him. In 1817 their remains, as is generally believed, were moved to Père Lachaise cemetery, and by tradition people bring letters there.

Rilke wrote down the formula of the strong version eight centuries later. In a letter to Emanuel von Bodman of 17 August 1901 he called a good marriage "that in which each appoints the other guardian of his solitude, and shows him this confidence, the greatest in his power to bestow". And he added that the measure for choosing a person must be "whether one is willing to stand guard over the solitude of a person and whether one is inclined to set this same person at the gate of one's own solitude, of which he learns only through that which steps, festively clothed, out of the great darkness".

Here is the 18-9-9 tail in one picture. The great darkness is The Moon of the entry. The solitude is The Hermit. The main task is to stand at the gate rather than move to another city, and to bring to the gate what was born in the dark. Abelard was at first a guardian who had left his post. With her letters Heloise brought him back to it.
What helps a couple with this tail:

ul: **Name the withdrawal.** "I need some time alone; it's not about us" — a silence with a name is not frightening.
**Don't take strength for having no needs.** Ask "how are you?" of exactly the one who always copes.
**Add a word to the deed.** A repair, a gift, a paid bill — and one sentence about why.
**Tell the partner about the trouble first, and a friend second.** Not the other way round.
**Keep a shared Paraclete.** A place or ritual where two silences meet: an evening walk, a weekly letter, a morning hour without phones.
**Keep the secret for two, and keep no secrets from each other about what matters.** The Moon of the entry is an alliance against the world, not a wall inside the couple.
**Don't put out the other's hermitage.** Among the tasks of a couple with The Hermit, Lisovskaya lists not extinguishing a partner's interest in their own pursuits.

paragraphs: If the silence in a couple rests on fear, bans or threats, it is no longer about the tail: it is a reason to call a local emergency number or crisis line, or to see a psychologist.

sections.h2: 18-9-9, 9-9-18 and 9-18-9: the same cards in a different order
paragraphs: The same numbers make two more couple tails. In 9-9-18 the couple enters the task through The Hermit, with a wish for quiet and space of its own, and the main task becomes The Moon: fears, invented stories, trust in what is left unsaid. It occurs in 3.26% of couples, and their centre is The Moon in 74% of cases.

In 9-18-9 the entry and the task are The Hermit, while the middle passes through The Moon: the path runs through fog, secrets and misunderstandings. That is 1.136% of couples, with The Moon in the centre in 81.3%. Only in 18-9-9 does the secret come at the start and the solitude in the lesson.
The personal karmic tail 18-9-9 is a different calculation with different roles for the points; the site has a separate article on it, and its conclusions do not carry over to the couple.

intro: The riddle of this tail is that a union in which two people understand each other without words is given words as its task. The three roles in brief:

ul: **18 · The Moon — entry to the task.** Where the couple starts and what it agrees on: a common language of hints and half-sentences, a world for two hidden from everyone else. The same wish for secrecy also becomes resistance: it is easier to keep quiet about what matters most.

**9 · The Hermit — middle of the task.** How the couple walks the path: each withdrawing into their own work, study, quiet or separate room. Distance can bring them closer here, but pauses easily turn into habit.
**9 · The Hermit — main task.** What the two have to learn: not to leave the other alone with their trouble, not to mistake a partner's strength for having no needs, and to put care into words.

intro: About one couple in 57 has this tail. Eight hundred years ago two people lived out its plot, Peter Abelard and Heloise, and she left the most precise words about it.

faq.q: What does the karmic tail 18-9-9 mean in compatibility?
faq.a: It is the tail of a couple's matrix: The Moon at the entry to the task, The Hermit in the middle and in the main task. The couple comes together over a shared secret and an understanding without words, walks the path with each withdrawing into their own, and the main task is to keep solitude from becoming silence: share troubles, ask the strong one too, add words to deeds.

faq.q: Is the 18-9-9 tail a bad sign for a couple?
faq.a: No. A couple's tail shows a task, not a rating of the union; the method gives no compatibility percentages. This tail's strength is right there in the cards: the two can be close without getting in each other's way, and they understand more than they say. The difficulty comes from the same source: silence is easy to mistake for calm.

faq.q: Does 18-9-9 mean the couple is destined to live apart?
faq.a: No. The cards predict neither partings nor moves. The Hermit in the middle and in the task speaks of how the couple walks its path and what it learns: to protect each partner's solitude while not leaving the other alone. The story of Abelard and Heloise is an example of the mechanism, not a forecast.

faq.q: Why is the centre of an 18-9-9 couple only The Moon or The Hermit?
faq.a: Because of the arithmetic of reduction. Adding digits does not change the remainder after division by nine, and by that remainder the couple's centre, entry, middle and values depend on the main task. If the task is The Hermit, they are all divisible by nine, and only two cards are: 9 and 18. In 57.1% of 18-9-9 couples the centre is The Moon, in 42.9% The Hermit.

faq.q: If one partner has the personal tail 18-9-9, is it the same thing?
faq.a: No. A personal tail is calculated from one date, and its points have different roles. A couple's tail is the sum of the points of two matrices. In 83% of couples with the 18-9-9 tail neither partner has The Moon or The Hermit in their personal tail: these cards appear only when the two are together.

faq.q: How is a couple's tail calculated?
faq.a: A personal matrix is calculated for each partner, then the matching points are added and the sum is reduced to 22. The entry to the task is the sum of the partners' entries, the middle the sum of their middles, the main task the sum of their main tasks. For example, 07.08.1976 and 05.07.1975 give 6 + 12 = 18, 8 + 19 = 27 → 9 and 20 + 7 = 27 → 9.

What helps a couple with this tail:

ul: name the withdrawal: "I need some time alone; it's not about us";
ask "how are you?" of exactly the one who always copes;
add a word to the deed — one sentence about why;
tell the partner about the trouble first, and a friend second;
keep a shared Paraclete — a walk, a letter, an hour without phones, where two silences meet.

report: If the silence in a couple rests on fear, bans or threats, it is no longer about the tail: it is a reason to call a local emergency number or crisis line, or to see a psychologist.

unit.title: A consolation sent to a friend

captions.M: To want a secret for two and understand without words
captions.N: To go each your own way while quiet is still a choice
captions.D: To ask “how are you?” of the one who always copes

unit.meaning: Your task is to guard each other's solitude but not fall silent: share trouble with your partner first, add words to deeds.
